meal.title: Avoid the missing ampersand mistake
meal.objective: Identify and fix the common error of forgetting the ampersand in scanf

voice.script: Why does my program crash after entering a number? Many beginners ask: Why does my program crash after I type a number? The problem is forgetting the ampersand in the input function. In C, scanf needs the address of a variable so it knows where to store the value. The ampersand operator gives that address. Without it, scanf writes to a random spot, causing crashes or garbage results. The correct pattern is: read an integer by writing ampersand before the variable name. Now see the correct line. When you run the program, it will wait for your numbers and then display the sum without crashing. Remember: always put an ampersand in front of each variable you read with scanf. Try fixing a broken program by adding the missing ampersand wherever scanf appears.
